_readme: Eight pages: a hub, one per grade (1-6), and Teacher Mode. Each carries
an empty themed container; assets/js/game-zone.js fills it from the JSON
in data/games/. Adding a game means editing data/games/grade-N.json —
no page here changes, and no JavaScript changes.
The 'styles' key loads assets/css/games.css on these pages only, so the
other 190 pages carry none of the Game Zone's weight.
Illustrations live in assets/img/games/ as original SVG artwork, about
0.6 KB each. Any picture named in a data file can be swapped for a
better one by replacing that file.

pages.title: Primary Game Zone
pages.metaTitle: Primary Game Zone | Games for Grades 1-6 | RCF English
pages.description: Colourful English games for Grades 1 to 6: picture matching, memory pairs, quizzes, sorting, sentence building and missing words. Free, and they work on a phone.
pages.keywords: English games for children Sri Lanka, primary English games, grade 1 english game, grade 6 english game, free english games for kids

hero.text: Six kinds of English game for Grades 1 to 6. Every game takes three to five minutes, works on a phone, and keeps your stars when you come back.

items.title: Pick your grade
items.text: Each grade has its own colour and its own games, from first words in Grade 1 to grammar puzzles in Grade 6.

items.title: Play for a few minutes
items.text: Every game is short. Wrong answers cost nothing: you simply try again until the sentence is right.

items.title: Collect your stars
items.text: Finish a game to earn up to three stars. Your stars stay on your own device. Nothing is sent anywhere and no account is needed.

blocks.title: For teachers
text: **Teacher Mode** opens any game large on a classroom screen: choose the grade, then the topic, then the game. Press Escape to come back to the list.
The games need no login, no plugin and no connection once the page has loaded, so they work on a school projector or a phone passed around a group.

items.title: Open Teacher Mode
items.text: Grade, then topic, then game — opened large for the class.

blocks.heading: Which grade to choose
text: Choose the grade the child is in now, not the grade of the words they already know. The games follow the Pupil's Book themes for each grade, so a child playing their own grade meets the words their class is using that term.
If the games for their grade are too hard, go down one: the themes repeat from year to year, so nothing is missed. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone,** and no account is needed.

pages.title: Grade 1 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 1 English Games | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Free Grade 1 English games: match animals and colours to their words, find memory pairs, and name shapes and first sounds. No reading needed, and no adverts.

hero.text: Pictures, first words and sounds. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 66 games here across 16 themed units, about 3.6 hours of play in all, covering the sixteen themes of the Grade 1 year - the school, the home, animals in the garden, water, the sky, food and drink, transport, light, and the people who help us.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
The games follow the themes of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Book for the grade, so a child plays the words they are meeting in class that term.

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **First words, with pictures.** Every word is shown as a picture before it is shown as writing, so a child who cannot yet read can still play.
**Greeting and naming.** *Hello, I'm ... What's your name? Thank you. Good morning.* - said, heard and matched, not written.
**Colours, shapes and first sounds,** which are what Grade 1 spends its year on.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: A six-year-old works best in one short go. One topic, five minutes, then stop while it is still fun. Coming back tomorrow teaches far more than pushing on today.

pages.title: Grade 2 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 2 English Games | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Grade 2 English games: match everyday things to their words, find memory pairs, finish short sentences and build them word by word.

hero.text: Pictures and short sentences you can read. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 75 games here across 16 themed units, about 4.2 hours of play in all, covering the sixteen Grade 2 themes, which revisit the Grade 1 topics and take each one further.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
The games follow the themes of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Book for the grade, so a child plays the words they are meeting in class that term.

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **The same themes, a year on.** School, home, animals, water, the sky, food, transport: the words a child met in Grade 1 come back with more of them, and in short sentences rather than single words.
**Polite English:** *Good morning, sir. Excuse me. Here are ... I'm from ...*
**Putting words in order,** which is new this year - eleven of the games ask a child to build a sentence rather than only recognise a word.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Grade 2 children will play longer than Grade 1 children, but ten minutes is still the right length. If a game is too easy, it is: move to the next theme rather than finishing every game in order.

pages.title: Grade 3 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 3 English Games | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Free Grade 3 English games: singular and plural, sorting animals into groups, and putting sentences in order. Tied to the Pupil's Book themes, and ad-free.

hero.text: More words, plurals and sentences that grow. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 46 games here across 8 themed units, about 2.6 hours of play in all, covering the eight Grade 3 themes - yourself, your home, your school, food, animals, clothes, play, and the world around you.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
The games follow the themes of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Book for the grade, so a child plays the words they are meeting in class that term.

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **Talking about yourself:** *I'm ... I'm seven. I live in ... This is my ...* - the questions a child is asked first, and often cannot answer.
**He and she,** which Sinhala and Tamil speakers mix up for years unless it is practised early.
**Numbers, and reading short written words** rather than only matching pictures.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Grade 3 is where reading starts to matter. Let the child read the word aloud before tapping, even when tapping the picture would be quicker. The extra two seconds are the whole point.

blocks.heading: What comes next
text: Grade 3 is the year reading begins to carry the weight. When a child can read the words in these games without looking at the pictures, they are ready for [Grade 4](primary-english/game-zone/grade-4/), where sentences have to be built rather than chosen.
For written practice alongside the games, the [primary English pages](primary-english/) have worksheets for the same themes.

pages.title: Grade 4 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 4 English Games | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Grade 4 English games: naming, doing and describing words, choosing the right verb, opposites, and rebuilding longer sentences.

hero.text: Word classes, verbs and longer sentences. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 47 games here across 10 themed units, about 2.8 hours of play in all, covering the ten Grade 4 themes - family and friends, the garden, places around you, work, festivals, shopping, the calendar, games, good practices and happy days.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
The games follow the themes of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Book for the grade, so a child plays the words they are meeting in class that term.

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **There is and there are,** and **this, that, these and those** - small words that decide whether a sentence sounds right.
**Describing:** parts of the body, what a plant has, what a place looks like. Grade 4 is the year a child stops naming things and starts describing them.
**Days, months and dates,** which are needed for everything afterwards and are learnt fastest by repetition.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Eight of the games at this grade ask for word order. Those are the ones worth repeating: understanding a sentence is easier than building one, and only building it proves the child can use it.

pages.title: Grade 5 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 5 English Games | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Grade 5 English games: reading comprehension, prepositions and tenses, word groups, vocabulary pairs and long sentence building.

hero.text: Reading, grammar and Scholarship-style challenges. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 43 games here across 10 themed units, about 2.7 hours of play in all, covering the ten Grade 5 themes - Sri Lanka, nature, caring and sharing, celebrations, sport, healthy living, the fair, safety, the wider world and the future.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
The games follow the themes of the Sri Lankan Pupil's Book for the grade, so a child plays the words they are meeting in class that term.

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **A, an and the,** which have no equivalent in Sinhala or Tamil and are the commonest mistake in Sri Lankan English writing at every later grade.
**Talking about where you are from:** province, town, country - the questions a Grade 5 child meets in the scholarship examination and in any conversation with a stranger.
**Longer sentences,** built rather than chosen: fourteen of the games at this level are quizzes on meaning rather than matching on pictures.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Grade 5 is a scholarship year for many children and the temptation is to use screen time for past papers. Ten minutes of these games is still worth it: vocabulary is the one thing no amount of paper practice supplies.

pages.title: Grade 6 Games
pages.metaTitle: Grade 6 English Games | Grammar Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Free Grade 6 English grammar games: sort common and proper nouns, choose is/are/was/were, pick a/an/the, place and time prepositions, and rebuild sentences. Drag-and-drop and word-order puzzles, ad-free.
pages.keywords: grade 6 english games, grade 6 grammar games, nouns verbs articles prepositions, drag and drop english, sentence building grade 6

hero.text: Grammar puzzles for Grade 6: nouns, be-verbs, articles, prepositions and sentence order. Tap a game to start.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: There are 12 short grammar games across five topics — about an hour of play in all — covering the same focuses as the Grade 6 grammar worksheets: common and proper nouns, *is / are / was / were*, *a / an / the*, and prepositions of place and time.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**
Pupil's Book unit games for Grade 6 will be added when the 2026 book units are mapped. Until then, these practice games sit beside the skill activities on the [Grade 6 English page](grades/grade-6/).

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **Sorting and drag-and-drop.** Nouns into common or proper; phrases into place or time; *a* versus *an* by sound.
**Missing-word gaps** for *is / are / was / were* and for articles and prepositions — the same choices children meet on paper.
**Sentence order puzzles**, so a child builds the sentence rather than only recognising it.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Use one topic after the matching worksheet, or before a term test. Ten minutes of sorting nouns or rebuilding sentences is enough for one sitting; stars stay on the device so coming back tomorrow continues the same progress.
For reading a timetable, filling in a form, and the poem activities on the 2026 syllabus, open the [Grade 6 practice page](grades/grade-6/#practice).

pages.title: Teacher Mode
pages.metaTitle: Teacher Mode | Primary Game Zone | RCF English
pages.description: Choose a grade, a topic and a game, and open it large on a classroom screen. No login and no connection needed once the page has loaded.

hero.text: Choose a grade, then a topic, then a game. It opens large enough for the back of the room. Press Escape to come back.

blocks.heading: What is in here
text: This page gathers every game in the Primary Game Zone, in one place, arranged so a teacher can find one quickly.
Everything is free, needs no account, and works on a phone. **There is no advertising anywhere in the Game Zone.**

blocks.heading: What it practises
bullets: **Choose by grade or by theme.** If today's lesson is about food, the food games from every grade are two taps away.
**Project it, or pass a phone round.** The games are built for a phone screen, so they work on a classroom projector and on the one device in the room.
**No sound is needed.** Every game can be played silently, which matters in a classroom of forty.

blocks.heading: Getting the most from it
text: Use a game to start a lesson rather than to end it. Five minutes of a matching game on the words you are about to teach puts those words in front of the class before the lesson needs them - which is worth more than the same five minutes spent as a reward at the end.
